name: aj-tools-aj-ai-mcp
description: MCP server that lets an AI agent run C# against a live Revit document through the AJ Tools AJ AI bridge, for automated tool testing/debugging. v1.3.0 adds 14 typed, schema-validated native tools (list/count/hide/isolate/unhide/reset-isolation/set-color/reset-overrides/transparency/select/set-parameter/report-parameters/move/delete) alongside the original run_csharp/ping/model_summary. v1.3.1 adds the npm-test smoke suite, set_parameter_value input validation, and discovery-file error hardening. v1.5.0 supports more than one Revit at a time: each session hosts its own pipe and is discovered from %APPDATA%/AJTools/bridges, with list_revit_instances and use_revit_instance to see and choose between them. One Revit open behaves exactly as before; with two or more nothing is sent until one is chosen. v1.6.0 adds run_fragment: run the proven scripts/ library by name with its INPUTS filled in and type-checked, composed per scripts/README.md, instead of pasting a hand-edited copy into run_csharp. v1.7.0 makes the server work on every Revit from 2020 to 2027: the generated C# no longer names DisplayUnitType (removed after 2020, which had left model_summary and move_elements dead on 2024+ and twelve more tools dead on any mm filter) and resolves ElementId.Value/.IntegerValue by reflection so 64-bit ids stop failing silently. tools/check-scripts.cmd now compile-checks the generated C# alongside scripts/ - the gap that let both survive. Also: every tool declares readOnly/destructive/idempotent/openWorld annotations from one table in shared/register.js, registration moved off the deprecated server.tool() to registerTool, the reported version is read from this file instead of being repeated in index.js, and the Brain search tools no longer block the event loop.
